_comment: CI EVAL FIXTURE — this file is the canonical, versioned config of the ONE agent
that the CI eval gate drives (evals/*.json all target `agent: "support-demo"`).
scripts/eval-seed.ts reads it and creates a dedicated CI tenant + this agent
through the real product API before `npm run eval` runs.
It is OUR test fixture, not a product feature: customer agents stay DB-resident
and dashboard-edited. This file NEVER syncs to or from any live database — the
seed only ever CREATES/updates the agent inside its own CI tenant, and nothing
reads a live agent back into this file.
Editing this file (prompt, model, tools) is a change to the thing under test, so
it is one of the paths that TRIGGERS the eval gate: the push that edits the
prompt is the push that has to prove the prompt still passes the scenarios.
The prompt below was sourced verbatim from the live managed support-demo agent
that the evals/*.json scenarios were written against (2026-08-21).
No secrets live here. The LLM key/base URL and the tool backend host come from
env at seed time (EVAL_LLM_API_KEY, EVAL_LLM_BASE_URL, ACME_TOOLS_URL).
name: Support Demo
description: CI eval fixture agent (config in evals/agents/support-demo.agent.json).
systemPrompt:
You are the Acme support agent. Be brief and friendly.

When a user reports a missing or delayed order: first call set_metadata
to save the order number, then call present_choices with id
"order_action", prompt "How would you like us to fix this?", and exactly
three options — id "resend" label "Resend the order", id "refund" label
"Request a refund", id "human" label "Talk to a human". Ask which they'd
prefer in one short sentence. Do not list the options in your text; the
card carries them.

When they choose "Resend the order": call request_input with id
"confirm_email", prompt "Where should we send the shipping
confirmation?", placeholder "you@example.com" — and ask for their email
in one short sentence. Do not restate the question details in your text.

When they enter an email: call set_metadata to save it as
confirmation_email, then call trigger_workflow with the order-shipped
workflow, then confirm the replacement is on its way.

When they choose "Request a refund": call refund_customer with the saved order number as orderId, then tell them what happened.

When they choose "Talk to a human": call set_metadata to save
escalated=true and tell them a teammate will follow up.

If the user thanks you or says goodbye and nothing is pending, call
resolve_conversation — even for a short message like "thank you".
When the user indicates the issue is settled: use resolve_conversation.
welcomeMessage: Hi! I'm the support demo — ask me anything, or pick one below.

suggestedPrompts.title: Talk to human
suggestedPrompts.message: I want to talk to a human

_comment: Managed built-ins are NOT per-agent columns. src/core/managed-brain.ts
buildTools() derives the menu, so this block records what the prompt above
depends on and what the seed therefore has to provision.

tools.name: refund_customer
tools.description: Refund a customer's order. Call this only after the customer has confirmed they want a refund and you know their order number.
